title: Silence-Conditional Output Suppression for Training-Free Whisper Hallucination Mitigation

contributions.purpose: Mitigate Whisper hallucinations on non-speech audio without fine-tuning or external components.
contributions.mechanism: Silence-Conditional Output Suppression: extract Whisper's internal no-speech probability (p_no_speech) from the first decoder step and, when p_no_speech >= threshold tau, output an empty transcription; otherwise proceed with standard greedy decoding.
contributions.evaluation: On UrbanSound8K, hallucination rate drops from 100% to 60.11% at tau=0.3 (a 39.9pp reduction).
contributions.source_quote: A training-free method for Whisper hallucination mitigation that leverages the model's internal p_no_speech signal, requiring no fine-tuning or external components.

contributions.purpose: Show the method preserves speech recognition quality while reducing hallucinations.
contributions.mechanism: Evaluate the hallucination-WER tradeoff on UrbanSound8K vs LibriSpeech across thresholds tau in {0.3, 0.5, 0.6}, comparing to default Whisper and an Always-Mask head-masking baseline.
contributions.evaluation: At tau=0.3, WER impact is +0.19pp on LibriSpeech test-clean (2.83->3.02) and 0 on test-other (5.10 unchanged), with a 0.19% false-positive rate (5/2620).
contributions.source_quote: Comprehensive evaluation showing 39.9 percentage point hallucination reduction (100% → 60.1%) on UrbanSound8K with minimal WER impact (+0.19 percentage points on LibriSpeech test-clean, 0 on test-other).

contributions.purpose: Characterize when the method works and when it fails.
contributions.mechanism: Per-class trigger-rate analysis at tau=0.5 across the 10 UrbanSound8K sound classes.
contributions.evaluation: High trigger rate on non-speech-like sounds (gun_shot 88.8%) but very low on speech-like audio (street_music 1.5%, children_playing 3.9%), explaining the residual 60% hallucination rate.
contributions.source_quote: Analysis revealing class-dependent effectiveness: the method works well on non-speech-like sounds (88.8% trigger rate on gun_shot) but struggles with speech-like environmental audio (1.5% on street_music).

contributions.purpose: Establish which component actually drives the improvement.
contributions.mechanism: Skip-Only ablation that applies the p_no_speech suppression policy but uses standard (unmasked) decoding for non-triggered clips.
contributions.evaluation: At tau=0.6, Skip-Only is identical to the full method (78.37% hallucination, 2.86% test-clean WER, 5.10% test-other), confirming the suppression policy, not decoder head masking, drives the gains.
contributions.source_quote: Ablation study confirming that the suppression policy, not decoder head masking, drives the hallucination reduction.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Most closely related to our work, Wang et al. (2025) identify that a small subset of decoder self-attention heads (heads {1, 6, 11}) account for over 75% of hallucinations on non-speech audio ... Our work builds on their mechanistic insight but takes a different approach: rather than modifying decoder computation, we leverage Whisper's internal p_no_speech signal to conditionally suppress output.
Our work applies this head-level understanding to ASR hallucination mitigation, though our ablation reveals that the suppression policy, not head masking, drives our method's effectiveness.
Whisper's multitask training format includes a special <|nospeech|> token that the model is trained to predict when audio contains no speech ... which we denote as p_no_speech.

notes: Residual hallucination rate stays high (60.1% at tau=0.3); the borrowed head-masking mechanism from Wang et al. (2025) is shown to contribute nothing (Always-Mask degrades WER without reducing hallucination), so the paper is largely a negative/trade-off result on that component.
